title: Scyther Is Flying-Type, But Rarely Flies
premise: Scyther has the Flying type, yet its Pokédex says it very rarely spreads its wings to fly.
audiencePromise: Show why Scyther feels more like a grounded ninja than an airborne Pokémon.
openLoop: If Scyther rarely flies, what makes it feel so dangerous?
payoff: Scyther's Flying type clashes with its real style: hide, dash, and slice from the ground.
engagementQuestion: Grounded ninja or reluctant flyer—which fits Scyther better?

voice.instructions: Speak quickly, warmly, and clearly. Stress Flying-type, rarely, blur, and grounded. Pause briefly before the final choice.

scenes.headline: FLYING-TYPE. RARELY FLIES.
scenes.narration: Scyther is Flying-type—but almost never flies.
scenes.caption: FLYING-TYPE • RARELY FLIES

scenes.headline: A BLUR, THEN A SLICE
scenes.narration: Its real threat is speed: a blur, then the scythes arrive.
scenes.caption: TOO FAST TO TRACK

scenes.headline: THE GRASS HIDES IT
scenes.narration: In grass, its protective colors can make Scyther invisible.
scenes.caption: HIDE FIRST. STRIKE FAST.

scenes.headline: HIDE. DASH. SLICE.
scenes.narration: So its battle style looks grounded: hide, dash, and slice.
scenes.caption: GROUND-LEVEL NINJA MOVEMENT

scenes.headline: THE FLYING TYPE REMAINS
scenes.narration: The Pokédex still calls it Flying-type; it just rarely spreads wings.
scenes.caption: FLYING DOESN'T MEAN CONSTANT FLIGHT

scenes.headline: NINJA OR FLYER?
scenes.narration: Grounded ninja or reluctant flyer—which fits Scyther better?
scenes.caption: CHOOSE SCYTHER'S TRUE STYLE
